title: Wendy’s Mom’s Dumplings

items.raw: 1 pound (450 g) ground pork, not lean
3 cups finely chopped napa cabbage (about ½ small head)
1 teaspoon kosher salt, for the cabbage
1 tablespoon Shaoxing wine or dry sherry
40 round dumpling wrappers, store-bought — or Wendy’s mom’s homemade wrapper
3 tablespoons soy sauce, 2 tablespoons black or rice vinegar, 1 teaspoon chili oil, slivered ginger

steps.text: Toss the chopped cabbage with the salt and let it sit 15 minutes. Then squeeze it hard in a towel to remove as much water as you can. Wet cabbage makes soggy dumplings that will not seal.

Put the pork in a bowl with the soy sauce, wine, sesame oil, ginger, and white pepper. Stir hard in one direction with chopsticks for 2 minutes until it turns sticky and springy. Fold in the cabbage and scallions.
Hold a wrapper in your palm and put about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center. Wet half the edge with water with your fingertip.

Fold the wrapper over into a half-moon and pinch the top center closed. Then make 3 or 4 small pleats along the front edge on each side, pressing each pleat against the flat back. Press out any air. Set on a floured tray, not touching.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high. Arrange dumplings flat side down and fry 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden. Add ⅓ cup water, cover immediately, and steam 6 minutes. Uncover and cook until the water is gone and the bottoms re-crisp, 1 to 2 minutes.
Drop into a large pot of boiling water. When it returns to a boil, add 1 cup cold water; repeat twice more. They are done when they float and the wrappers are tender, about 6 to 8 minutes total.
Stir the dipping sauce ingredients together and serve with the dumplings hot.

notes.label: Test the seasoning
notes.text: fry a small spoonful of filling and taste it before folding forty dumplings.

notes.label: Freezing
notes.text: freeze on the floured tray until hard, then bag. Cook straight from frozen, adding 2 minutes of steaming.

notes.label: Keep wrappers covered
notes.text: they dry out within minutes. Keep the stack under a damp towel.

notes.label: Variations
notes.text: add a handful of chopped shiitake or garlic chives to the filling.

openQuestion: This is a best guess — pork and napa cabbage dumplings, pan-fried or boiled. Tell me about Wendy’s mom and these dumplings: what is in her filling, how she folds them, whether she boils or pan-fries, and whether she makes the wrappers or buys them. Her dipping sauce, too.
